title: Little Shop of Horrors praised as exceptionally crafted feelgood movie
content:
In a new series highlighting writers’ favorite comfort films, a feature explores why the 1980s musical Little Shop of Horrors serves as a quintessential feelgood movie. The article argues that the key to such films is familiarity, which allows viewers to look away or fall asleep without losing affection for the story. Musicals are described as particularly suited to this subgenre, though many classic film adaptations suffer from second-act issues where the plot takes precedence over the musical elements.

The text contrasts this with the first act of Funny Girl, which is noted for its near-flawless sequence of showstoppers featuring Barbra Streisand as Fanny Brice. The author states they have likely seen Funny Girl 200 times but dismisses the second act, specifically citing a lack of interest in the character’s husband’s gambling addiction.
summary: The writer calls Little Shop of Horrors an exceptionally crafted feelgood movie. The article is part of a series celebrating writers’ favorite comfort films and highlights the lovably quirky 80s musical.
author: Guardian Culture

title: John Oliver calls underfunded Secret Service 'actively reckless' ahead of 2028
content:
John Oliver examined the Secret Service’s current challenges on the latest episode of Last Week Tonight, highlighting concerns about the agency’s funding and insular culture. The host described the agency as “actively reckless” in its approach to an upcoming period he and some agents have termed “Armageddon.” This 2028 timeframe will require the Secret Service to simultaneously staff the Los Angeles Olympics and Paralympics, the annual United Nations General Assembly, and provide security for the two presidential candidates and their families during the election.

Oliver also criticized the agency’s recruitment strategy, noting that it hired director Michael Bay to create a Super Bowl advertisement. The commercial, which asserted that “protectors are born, not made,” featured a photograph from the July 2024 rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, where President Trump was shot in the ear. Oliver remarked on the choice of imagery, stating, “That is not exactly a triumphant moment for them, is it?” and added, “It’s a bit odd to choose to self-promote using an image of yourself at your lowest.”
summary: John Oliver investigated the Secret Service's funding shortages and insular culture, highlighting the agency's challenging 2028 schedule. The segment criticized the agency's Super Bowl recruitment ad for using an image from the 2024 rally where Trump was shot.
author: Guardian Culture

title: What to do if you missed out on Glastonbury tickets
content: Fans who failed to secure a Glastonbury ticket during Sunday's sales should not lose hope, as alternative methods remain available to obtain entry. While the initial opportunity has passed, other avenues exist for those still seeking to attend the event.
summary: Those who missed out on Sunday should not lose hope, as there are other ways to secure a ticket.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: ICC delays plans for World Club Championship after ‘Big Three’ object
content:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) has postponed plans for a World Club Championship and other international multilateral tournaments until 2031 at the earliest due to objections from England, Australia, and India. These three nations stated that there is no space for extra events in the current schedule.

Following months of informal discussions between the ICC and member boards, a cricket operations workshop held in Dubai last week concluded without proposing any additional events. Consequently, the next Future Tours Programme (FTP), which will cover the period from 2027 to 2031, is expected to mirror the structure of the current cycle.
summary: England, Australia and India say no space for extra eventsNo new international tournaments until 2031 at earliestThe International Cricket Council (ICC) will not introduce a World Club Championship or more international multilateral tournaments until 2031 at the earliest because of resistance from England, Australia and India. After informal discussions between the ICC and member boards over several months, a cricket ­operations workshop in Dubai last week concluded without any ­additional events being proposed.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Coach Omits Jake Connor from Rugby League World Cup Squad
content:
Brian McDermott, the England head coach, has defended the omission of Leeds Rhinos half-back Jake Connor from the Rugby League World Cup squad, stating that the selected players are best suited to his gameplan for defeating top global opponents. Connor, who won the Super League’s Man of Steel award, is the second consecutive year to be a major talking point due to his exclusion, having also been left out by Shaun Wane for last autumn’s Ashes series.

The current squad notably includes Hull KR’s Lewis but contains no players from the new Super League champions, Wakefield. England lost the previous Ashes series 3-0 following a series of limited attacking displays.
summary: England head coach Brian McDermott omitted Leeds Rhinos half‑back Jake Connor from the Rugby League World Cup squad, saying the selected players better fit his game plan. Connor, who won Super League’s Man of Steel award, was also left out of the Ashes squad by Shaun Wane.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Daryz owner Zahra Aga Khan questions future after Arc win
content:
Princess Zahra Aga Khan, owner of Arc winner Daryz, addressed the question of the horse’s future following the achievement of back-to-back victories. While the win secured an unprecedented third title for the owners, the owner indicated that the team is considering the horse’s next steps rather than committing to an additional year of racing.

During the post-race press conference, Princess Zahra stated that as breeders, they accept the risks involved in running the horse. She expressed uncertainty about whether they would want Daryz to train for another year, suggesting instead that the horse likely has other purposes beyond continued competition.
summary: Princess Zahra Aga Khan stated that she is unsure if Daryz will train for another year following his back-to-back Arc victories. She noted that the decision involves risk and suggested the horse may have other roles beyond racing.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Anthony Barry says new structure frees England attackers after 7‑0 win over Croatia
content:
Assistant coach Anthony Barry said the new structure for England’s attack will keep key players “not caged in” after the team’s 7‑0 rout of Croatia.  

Barry has spent time reviewing the match debriefs and discussing details with head coach Thomas Tuchel, even joking that “he’s doing my head in.”  He asks what the missing piece is after England’s emotional semi‑final finish at the World Cup.  

The early Nations League campaign is viewed by the Football Association as a slingshot into Euro 2028, which England will co‑host.  Barry says the answer lies in liberation, allowing England’s top players to fully express themselves, and he highlights Jude Bellingham as the player who will benefit most.  

Barry believes this approach will unlock Bellingham’s full potential.
summary: Assistant coach Anthony Barry says England's new structure frees key attackers after a 7‑0 rout of Croatia. He says this liberation will let players like Jude Bellingham fully express themselves, helping England in the Nations League and towards Euro 2028.
author: Guardian Sport

title: F1 looks amateurish and incompetent after farcical scenes in Sepang
content:
A review of Formula One regulations is underway following a series of controversial incidents this season. The review focuses on misconceived regulations that have prevented cars from running in the rain, a problem that has drawn criticism from the drivers.

Drivers have also voiced overwhelming disapproval of the current engine regulations, despite the sport’s claim that the new format is more popular than ever. The farcical scenes that accompanied the opening to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday were highly visible and left some drivers expressing open mockery.

The review will address these issues.
summary: Review is underway, but there will be no quick fix for misconceived regulations that resulted in cars being unable to run in the rain. The farcical scenes at the opening of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday left some drivers expressing open mockery.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Medvedev Disqualified from China Open Semi After Hitting Fan With Ball
content:
Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from the China Open semi‑final against Novak Djokovic on Monday after a rebounding ball struck a spectator in the eye. The Russian, ranked world No. 5, was trailing 7‑5, 5‑3 and had lost a point when, in frustration, he struck a ball that had come off the back wall. The spectator, seated in the first row, clutched his left eye and left the gallery in pain, assisted by stadium staff.

Djokovic’s opponent was eliminated, and Djokovic now advances to the final where he will face Cameron De Minaur.
summary: Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from the China Open semi‑final against Novak Djokovic after striking a rebounding ball into the crowd that hit a spectator in the eye. The Russian, who was trailing 7‑5, 5‑3, hit the ball after losing a point, and the injured spectator left the gallery with assistance from stadium staff.
author: Guardian Sport

title: France beat Belgium 4-1 in Nations League, Olise scores four in 14 minutes
content:
France secured a 4‑1 victory over Belgium in the Nations League at the Stade de France, with Michael Olise coming off the bench to inspire the win. The match began with Belgium taking the lead when Dodi Lukébakio fired the visitors in front in the first half, marking Belgium’s first competitive win over France in 45 years.  

France responded with a blistering finish, scoring four goals in 14 minutes to preserve Zinedine Zidane’s unbeaten start at home and move closer to the quarter‑finals. The rapid turnaround erased Belgium’s early advantage and cemented the hosts’ dominance in the game.  

The Nations League roundup also included Italy’s victory over Turkey and Hungary edging out Ukraine, though specific match details were not provided.
summary: France won 4-1 over Belgium in the Nations League, with Michael Olise scoring four goals in a 14‑minute burst. The victory gave Zinedine Zidane his first home win since taking charge and kept him unbeaten as France move closer to the quarter‑finals.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Liam Gallagher defends Manchester City fans amid scandal backlash
content:
In an article titled “How did some City fans become aggressive defenders of a nation state’s regime?” by Sean Ingle, the author examines how fandom has warped beyond previous boundaries in online spaces. The piece uses the Manchester City case as a key example, noting that the fallout from the biggest scandal in British football history is now heading into a second week.

A video of Liam Gallagher playing in a 1996 charity football match resurfaced on social media. In the clip, the Oasis singer is dressed in Manchester City blue and a bucket hat, but he appears to be in a fug of cigarettes and alcohol before striking a shot into the top corner. Since last week, Gallagher has been defending the honour of his club with a more aggressive tone, replying to rival fans who want City to lose all their trophies after being found guilty of all serious charges. His reply on social media was, “There all NEUROTIC little GIMPS,” a statement that became one of dozens of sweary, punchy, and often amusing responses.

The article notes that these responses are built on a solitary article of faith: that City will somehow find a way to wriggle free.
summary: Liam Gallagher, who appeared in a 1996 charity match wearing Manchester City blue, responded to rival fans by calling them "neurotic little gims" on social media. The backlash follows Manchester City's guilty verdict on serious charges in the biggest scandal in British football history.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Juventus and Atletico Madrid target Arsenal forward Noni Madueke
content:
Arsenal forward Noni Madueke is attracting interest from clubs in Spain and Italy, with Juventus and Atletico Madrid among the suitors, according to Tuesday’s gossip.  

Five Premier League clubs have expressed interest in Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, while England captain Harry Kane is reportedly close to signing a new deal with Bayern Munich.  

The gossip also mentions additional developments.
summary: Arsenal forward Noni Madueke has suitors in Spain and Italy. Five Premier League clubs are interested in Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, and England captain Harry Kane is close to signing a new deal at Bayern Munich.

title: ECB to consider funding women's West Indies Test to aid Ashes prep
content: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said it will “look at” the unusual step of funding a women’s Test match in the West Indies next year. The move is intended to help England prepare for the upcoming Ashes series.
summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) will look at the unusual step of funding a women's Test in the West Indies next year. This would be to aid England’s Ashes preparations.

title: JJ Gabriel appears in Manchester United team photo despite ongoing rift
content:
Gabriel appears in a Manchester United team photograph, yet the image offers no indication that relations between the club and the player have improved.  

As he prepares to celebrate his 16th birthday, the ongoing rift between Manchester United and JJ Gabriel shows no sign of being healed.  

The presence of Gabriel in the photo does not signal any reconciliation between the parties.
summary: JJ Gabriel is featured in a Manchester United team photo. As he prepares to celebrate his 16th birthday, the rift between Manchester United and JJ Gabriel shows no sign of being healed.

title: Democratic super PAC pulls North Carolina ads as Roy Cooper leads Senate race
content: WinSenate, a super PAC linked to Senate Democratic leadership, is removing advertisements in North Carolina this week. The decision includes pulling approximately $500,000 in television advertising and $50,000 in digital advertising. A source familiar with the matter confirmed the move to The Hill, noting that recent polls show Democratic Senate candidate Roy Cooper holding a significant lead over Republican opponent Michael Whatley.
summary: A super PAC linked to Senate Democratic leadership is pulling down approximately $550,000 in TV and digital ads in North Carolina. This decision follows polls showing Democratic Senate candidate Roy Cooper with a healthy lead over Republican Michael Whatley.

title: Pennsylvania records over 1,000 measles cases amid outbreak
content:
Pennsylvania measles cases pass 1,000 mark amid outbreak

Pennsylvania has recorded more than 1,000 measles cases this year, surpassing the outbreaks in other states by hundreds. The state’s Department of Health dashboard, updated Monday, lists a total of 1,004 measles cases in Pennsylvania.

The report also notes 198 hospitalizations and five deaths related to the disease, underscoring the severity of the current outbreak.
summary: Pennsylvania has recorded 1,004 measles cases this year, with 198 hospitalizations and five deaths. This total surpasses the measles outbreaks in other states by hundreds.

title: Trump says he will ‘certainly look at’ U. S. military base in Lithuania
content:
President Trump stated on Monday that he will “certainly look at” establishing a U.S. military base in Lithuania. This comment came one week after the Lithuanian prime minister indicated that the country would welcome U.S. service members into the Baltic state.

Addressing the potential base, the president described the Lithuanians as “friends of mine” and “great people.” He concluded by affirming, “so we’ll certainly look at it.”
summary: President Trump said Monday he will “certainly look at” establishing a U. S. Military base in Lithuania. This follows Lithuania’s prime minister saying he would welcome U. S. Service members into the Baltic state.
author: The Hill

title: Trump expresses concern over suspected Russian plague case
content:
President Trump expressed concern on Monday regarding a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia, stating that the U.S. is “looking at it very strongly.” He told reporters before departing the White House, “I hate to see them having it.”

The State Department confirmed on Monday that it is monitoring the suspected plague case in the Russian region.
summary: President Trump said the U.S. is looking at the suspected pneumonic plague case in Russia. The State Department is monitoring the suspected case in Irkutsk Oblast.

title: Vance and Cruz clash signals GOP gloves coming off in 2028 primary
content: Vice President Vance and Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) have engaged in increasingly personal exchanges, signaling that the 2028 Republican primary is officially underway and that political decorum is fading. The conflict initiated when Vance criticized Cruz, stating it was “really obvious” regarding the Texas senator’s positions. This development suggests that the gloves are coming off in the upcoming presidential contest.
summary: Vice President Vance and Sen. Ted Cruz
author: The Hill

title: Reflection AI releases first open-weight model Beam, says it rivals China
content:
Reflection AI, an open‑source startup backed by Nvidia, announced on Monday the release of its first open‑weight model, Beam. In a blog post, the company said Beam is on par with leading open‑source models developed in the United States and China.

The startup claims that Beam rivals the top open technologies produced in both countries, positioning it as a competitive option in the AI model landscape. The announcement highlights Reflection AI’s goal of providing open‑source solutions that match the performance of major industry players.
summary: Reflection AI, an open-source startup backed by Nvidia, released its first open-weight model, Beam, on Monday. The company claims Beam is on par with leading open-source models made in China.
author: The Hill

title: Trump rallies Nebraska voters as GOP seeks to defend seat in competitive Senate race
content:
President Trump will rally voters in Nebraska Monday evening, as Republicans look to shore up support in a state where an unexpectedly competitive Senate race has put the GOP on defense.  

Sen. Pete Ricketts (R‑Neb.) is facing independent Dan Osborn in the Senate contest. Osborn came within 7 points of Sen. Deb Fischer (R‑Neb.) in 2024.  

The GOP is on defense in Nebraska.
summary: President Trump will hold a rally in Nebraska on Monday evening as Republicans seek to strengthen support amid a competitive Senate race. Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) faces independent Dan Osborn, who came within 7 points of Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) in 2024.

title: Rep. Crockett Endorses All Texas Democrats, Including James Talarico
content:
Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D‑Texas) announced that she supports every Democrat on the Texas ballot, including the Democratic Senate nominee who defeated her in the primary.  

In a livestream on social media, Crockett said, “I support all Democrats. Yes, that includes James Talarico, who I endorsed the day after the election, OK?” The statement came after Talarico won the Democratic nomination for the U.S. Senate seat.
summary: Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-Texas) said she supports all Democrats on the ballot in Texas. She added that this includes Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico, who defeated her in the primary, and she endorsed him the day after the election.
author: The Hill

title: Supreme Court Begins New Term with High‑Stakes Climate Case
content:
The Supreme Court’s new term began with a high‑profile climate change case that has already drawn national attention.

The case focuses on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change. The legal question centers on the extent of municipal authority in addressing environmental damage caused by major energy firms.

While the dispute is framed around climate impacts, the court notes that its outcome could have broader implications beyond the environmental sphere.
summary: The Supreme Court case examines whether local governments can hold large energy companies accountable for climate‑related local harms. The case also has implications beyond climate.
author: NPR Politics

title: No 10 says RAF Fairford remains safe after US bombers withdrawn
content:
No 10 has insisted that RAF Fairford remains safe after the United States withdrew its bombers from the base.  

US media reported that a new threat prompted the removal of the bombers on Sunday, following an incident near the base last week.
summary: No 10 says RAF Fairford remains safe after US bombers were removed. US media reported that a new threat led to the bombers being removed on Sunday following an incident near the base last week.
author: BBC Politics

title: First Minister O'Neill rejects call to resign over Drumcree row
content:
First Minister Michelle O'Neill rejected calls to resign over the Drumcree row.  She faced questions in the Stormont Assembly regarding the dispute.

During the session, O'Neill said she was “proud” to stand with the residents and that she would “continue to stand with them.”
summary: First Minister O'Neill rejected calls to resign over the Drumcree row. Facing questions in the Stormont assembly, she said she was proud to stand with the residents and will continue to stand with them.
author: BBC Politics

title: UN climate chief warns of heat threat to mothers and babies at pre‑COP
content:
UN climate chief warned that rising temperatures pose a heat threat to mothers and babies during the first day of the pre‑COP31 meeting in Fiji.  

The meeting’s opening day spotlighted maternal health, with Pacific concerns set to top the agenda as ministers gathered for talks.
summary: The UN climate chief warned that heat poses a threat to mothers and babies during the pre‑COP31 meeting in Fiji. The meeting highlighted maternal health and Pacific concerns, with ministers gathering for talks.
author: Climate Home News

title: Africa Must Address Colonial Extraction, Debt, and Inequality in Climate Adaptation
content:
Climate Home News published an opinion piece titled “Africa should not have to adapt to an unjust climate system.” The article argues that climate adaptation in Africa must move beyond building infrastructure and enhancing resilience.

According to the post, effective adaptation also needs to confront the legacy of colonial extraction, unequal development and debt dependency, which it says continue to heighten Africa’s vulnerability to climate impacts. The piece appeared first on Climate Home News.
summary: The article argues that Africa's climate adaptation must go beyond infrastructure and resilience to tackle colonial extraction, unequal development, and debt dependency. These factors continue to fuel Africa's vulnerability to climate impacts.
author: Climate Home News

title: Think tank says Tory energy rule cut would cost new homeowners £1,000 a year
content:
A researcher at a climate‑change think tank has warned that the Conservative government’s plan to reduce the energy‑efficiency rule for builders would cost new home buyers about £1,000 a year, calling the policy a “disaster for first‑time buyers.”  

In a separate political stunt, the Tories distributed “Bottler Burnham” bottles of water, labelled “0 % strength,” to mock the claim that Burnham had cancelled early‑election plans under pressure from the Conservatives. The bottles carry an image of Burnham created by Manchester artist Stan Chow. The move echoes a 2008 event in which the party gave journalists “Bottler Brown” beer to criticize Gordon Brown’s last‑minute withdrawal of early‑election plans.  

The think‑tank critic also noted the SNP’s ban on new nuclear energy in Scotland, arguing that no part of Great Britain should be excluded from plans for new nuclear renewal.
summary: A researcher at a climate change think tank said the Conservative plan to cut the energy efficiency rule for builders would be a disaster for first‑time buyers. The think tank estimates the change would cost new home owners £1,000 a year.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Snakes, bobcats, mountain lions: the secret animal world beneath the Hollywood sign
content:
The Hollywood sign, an international symbol of Los Angeles, sits atop Mount Lee in the heart of the city. From its perch the wind is quiet, and two red‑tailed hawks glide above, barely flapping as they coast the thermal air.

The sign’s giant letters stand beside a quiet landscape of homes that spread out beneath it. On a clear day the view extends across the sky to Catalina Island, located 10 miles out across the Pacific.

The sign is described as a hallmark of the region’s environmental richness.
summary: The Hollywood sign sits atop Mount Lee in Los Angeles, overlooking a quiet wind and two red‑tailed hawks flying above. From the sign, the view extends over blocks of homes and reaches Catalina Island 10 miles across the Pacific.
author: Guardian Environment

title: ACP Recommends Estrogen-Based Therapy as First-Line for Menopausal Vasomotor Symptoms
content:
The American College of Physicians (ACP) has issued a new clinical guideline recommending hormonal therapy as the first‑line treatment for menopausal vasomotor symptoms (VMS).  

According to the guideline, perimenopausal and postmenopausal females who experience hot flashes and night sweats should receive estrogen in combination with progestogen if they have a uterus, or estrogen monotherapy if they do not.  

The ACP’s recommendations were published in the journal Annals of Internal Medicine.
summary: The American College of Physicians recommends estrogen in combination with progestogen for females with a uterus or estrogen monotherapy for females without a uterus as first‑line treatment for perimenopausal and postmenopausal females experiencing hot flashes and night sweats. The guideline was published in Annals of Internal Medicine.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UTSA study finds higher toxicants in autistic children’s baby teeth
content:
A pilot study conducted by The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center identified higher levels of toxicants in the primary teeth of children with autism. These elevated levels were observed when compared to the primary teeth of children without autism.

The toxicants detected in the study include compounds known to disrupt development or the endocrine system.
summary: A pilot study by The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center found elevated toxicant levels in the primary teeth of children with autism compared to children without autism. The study identified compounds that are known to disrupt development or the endocrine system.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cigarette smoke may prime lung stem cells for specific lung cancer types
content:
Chronic exposure to cigarette smoke can reprogram distinct populations of lung stem cells, which are responsible for maintaining and repairing lung tissue. This reprogramming renders these cells vulnerable to specific cancer-causing gene alterations.

Ultimately, the specific changes induced by smoke exposure help determine the particular type of lung cancer that develops in an individual.
summary: Chronic exposure to cigarette smoke may reprogram different populations of lung stem cells to make them vulnerable to specific cancer-causing gene alterations. This process may ultimately help determine the specific type of lung cancer that develops.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UA and Sant Joan d'Alacant Hospital launch MEL-IA AI for skin lesion classification
content:
The University of Alicante (UA) and the Sant Joan d'Alacant University Hospital have launched MEL-IA, an artificial intelligence system designed to automate the classification of skin lesions. This initiative aims to address the global health challenge of skin cancer, which saw nearly 1.5 million new cases diagnosed in 2024 according to World Health Organization (WHO) data.

The system, formally named MobilE skin Lesion dIAgnosis, has been integrated into hospital workflows to support the diagnostic process.
summary: The University of Alicante and Sant Joan d'Alacant University Hospital have launched MEL-IA, an AI system for automating skin lesion classification. The tool addresses the global skin cancer challenge, which saw nearly 1.5 million new cases in 2024, according to WHO.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Karolinska study links tumor cell spatial organization to patient outcomes
content:
New imaging method links cells' spatial organization to cancer outcomes

A doctoral thesis by Linglong Huang at the Karolinska Institutet's Department of Oncology‑Pathology suggests that the spatial organization of cells in solid tumors may provide clinically relevant information about patient outcomes. Huang’s research highlights that tumors are not composed solely of cancer cells; they also contain immune cells and other support cells that interact within a complex ecosystem known as the tumor microenvironment.
summary: Linglong Huang's doctoral thesis at Karolinska Institutet's Department of Oncology-Pathology suggests that the spatial organization of cells in solid tumors may provide clinically relevant information about patient outcomes. Tumors contain cancer cells, immune cells, and support cells that interact within a complex ecosystem known as the tumor microenvironment.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brain heartbeat responses differ in patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder
content:
Brain responses to heartbeat are altered in patients with iRBD

New research indicates that patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) exhibit altered brain responses to their heartbeat. iRBD is a condition marked by strong physical reactions to vivid, often violent dreams. It is recognized as one of the earliest warning signs of brain changes associated with Parkinson’s disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, sometimes appearing years before diagnosis.
summary: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder involves strong physical reactions to vivid, often violent dreams. It is one of the earliest warning signs of brain changes associated with Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies, sometimes appearing years before diagnosis.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Asymptomatic C. diff carriers drive most transmissions in cancer wards, study finds
content:
A new study modeling Clostridioides difficile (C. Diff) transmission in hospital cancer units found that most new infections are introduced by patients who are infected but not symptomatic at the time of admission.

Researchers modeled the spread of C. Diff among patients in oncology wards and determined that asymptomatic carriers at admission were the primary source of new cases, rather than patients who were infected and symptomatic.

The model offers a clearer picture of transmission events in oncology settings and could help inform protocols aimed at preventing future disease transmission in this highly susceptible population.
summary: Researchers modeled Clostridioides difficile (C. Diff) transmission among patients in hospital cancer units. The model found that most new infections were introduced by patients who were infected but not symptomatic at admission, rather than by symptomatic patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Airlines trim capacity amid rising jet fuel costs and steady bookings
content:
Airfares could rise even more, but airline profits won’t, according to recent industry observations.  

Airlines are trimming capacity as jet fuel prices keep climbing and travelers keep booking.  

The report notes that airlines are reducing capacity while fuel costs rise and demand remains strong.
summary: Airlines are trimming capacity as jet fuel prices keep climbing. Travelers continue to book flights.

title: David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz Announce Skydance Leadership Team
content:
David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz announced the leadership team for Skydance, the merged entity of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery.

The new team will oversee the combined operations of the two companies.  

The leadership roster will include Bari Weiss, Mark Thompson and Casey Bloys.

title: AstraZeneca CEO says Summit drug could drive next generation of cancer combinations after $2 billion investment
content:
Pascal Soriot, the chief executive of AstraZeneca, told CNBC that the company’s Summit drug could become a key driver of next‑generation cancer combinations after a $2 billion investment.  

Soriot made the comments from the site of AstraZeneca’s new $1 billion research and development facility in Kendall Square, Cambridge, Massachusetts.  

The company’s focus on the Summit drug and the substantial investment signal a continued push toward innovative cancer therapies.
summary: Pascal Soriot spoke exclusively with CNBC from the site of AstraZeneca's new $1 billion R&D facility in Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

title: Lucid Q3 deliveries drop 6.7% as production cut to 2,954 vehicles
content:
Lucid Group reported that third‑quarter deliveries fell 6.7%, reflecting a production cut aimed at matching demand.  

The automaker delivered 3,806 electric vehicles in the quarter and produced 2,954 units. By contrast, a year earlier Lucid delivered 4,078 vehicles and produced 3,891.  

The reduction in output underscores the company’s effort to align manufacturing levels with current market demand.
summary: Lucid delivered 3,806 EVs and produced 2,954 vehicles in the third quarter. That compares with 4,078 deliveries and 3,891 produced a year earlier.
author: CNBC Business

title: Trump’s recent economy comments spark expert concern over trade and AI policies
content:
Donald Trump used his Truth Social platform to claim that “the only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U. S. A. Has that, in spades!” The comment was part of a series of recent statements in which the president suggested the United States might cut off trade with “dozens of the US’s trading partners.”  

The remarks prompted a wave of criticism from economists and other experts, who said the proposals could pose a “clear and present danger” to both the U.S. and global economies. A Wall Street Journal poll cited in the article found that only 7 % of Americans believe Trump should lead efforts to regulate artificial intelligence.  

These reactions underscore growing skepticism about Trump’s economic judgment and the potential impact of his policy ideas.
summary: Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that the only guardrails AI needs are a “strong and smart (high IQ) president,” claiming the United States has that. He also floated the idea of cutting off trade with dozens of U.S. trading partners, leading experts to question his intelligence and warn the proposals could endanger the U.S. and world economies, while a WSJ poll found only 7% of Americans think he should lead AI regulation.
author: Guardian Business

title: Mark Thompson stays CEO of CNN after Paramount Skydance acquisition
content:
Mark Thompson announced in a memo to CNN staff on Monday that he will continue as chair and chief executive of the network after Paramount Skydance assumes control. Thompson, who has held the role since 2023, said the “specifics of how CNN will plug into and operate in the new company have yet to be finalized,” but he pledged to remain in his position.

The decision, made by Paramount Skydance chief executive David Ellison, was described as a relief to employees who had feared an overhaul and the possible appointment of Bari Weiss. The combined entity will be led by Ellison after the merger of Paramount Skydance with CNN’s parent, Warner Bros Discovery.

The transaction is expected to close formally on Tuesday.
summary: Mark Thompson, who has been chair and chief executive of CNN since 2023, said in a memo to staff that he will remain in his role after Paramount Skydance takes control of the network. The acquisition, which will merge Paramount Skydance with Warner Bros Discovery and be led by David Ellison, is expected to close on Tuesday.
author: Guardian Business

title: US Supreme Court hears oil companies' bid to block state climate lawsuits
content:
The U.S. Supreme Court opened its new nine‑month term on Monday by hearing arguments in a case that could halt state‑level lawsuits seeking to hold major oil producers accountable for climate damage.  

Suncor Energy and ExxonMobil argued that the lawsuits should be blocked, presenting their bid during an almost two‑hour hearing. The justices did not indicate a clear direction after the arguments.  

Legal experts said the Court may find it difficult to craft a majority opinion that sides with the industry, leaving the outcome uncertain.
summary: The US Supreme Court began its new nine‑month term hearing arguments from Suncor Energy and ExxonMobil seeking to stop state climate‑damage lawsuits. After an almost two‑hour hearing, it was unclear which way the justices were leaning, and experts said a majority decision favoring industry could be difficult.
author: Guardian Business

title: Average five-year mortgage rate reaches 6% for first time in three years
content:
The average five‑year mortgage rate has risen to 6%, marking the first time it has reached that level in three years.

The increase comes as the cost of a new fixed‑rate mortgage has been climbing in recent weeks, with lenders confronting higher expenses.
summary: The average five-year mortgage rate has risen to 6%, the first time it has reached that level in three years. The cost of new fixed-rate mortgages has been rising in recent weeks as lenders face higher costs.
author: BBC Business

title: Experts say bedside lumbar puncture training for neurologists is worthwhile
content:
Experts consider giving neurologists and neurology trainees the ability to perform lumbar punctures at the bedside a worthwhile objective.  

Point‑of‑care ultrasound (POCUS) is now required in many medical specialties for diagnosing patients and guiding procedures, and the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education lists proficiency in POCUS as an official graduation milestone. Training in POCUS for head, eye and nerve conditions is improving, though neurologists currently use the technology only moderately for certain neurological conditions.
summary: Experts consider enabling neurologists and neurology trainees to perform lumbar punctures at the bedside a worthwhile goal. Point‑of‑care ultrasound is now an ACGME graduation milestone, but neurologists use it only moderately despite improving training for head, eye and nerve conditions.
author: Phys.org

title: Long-term logging study finds forest floor protection preserves soil carbon
content:
A long‑term logging experiment has shown that keeping the forest floor intact can significantly reduce the loss of soil carbon when trees are harvested.  

Forest soils hold roughly 40 % of the world’s terrestrial carbon, yet studies estimate that harvesting a forest can release about 15 % to 30 % of that stored carbon.  

Researchers note that measuring these losses is complicated by factors such as wildfires, insect infestations, disease, previous forest‑management practices, as well as variations in tree species, climate and the specific harvesting methods used.  

The experiment’s findings suggest that protecting the forest floor during logging operations may help preserve a substantial portion of the carbon stored in forest soils.
summary: Forest soils store an estimated 40% of the world’s terrestrial carbon. Protecting the forest floor can help prevent the 15–30% soil carbon loss that typically occurs when a forest is harvested.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Mississippi study finds language linked to psychopathic traits is complex
content:
A recent University of Mississippi study indicates that the language linked to psychopathic traits is more complex than commonly portrayed.  

Popular culture often depicts individuals with psychopathy as cold, emotionless and hollow, but the research challenges that simplified image.  

The findings suggest that the linguistic patterns associated with psychopathic traits involve greater nuance than the stereotypical descriptions typically presented.
summary: Popular culture often portrays people with psychopathy as cold, emotionless and hollow. A recent University of Mississippi study found that the language associated with psychopathic traits is more complicated than commonly described.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers name new Cretaceous insect species Cretodorus noonoo from amber
content:
A fossilized insect trapped in amber has been identified as a new species from the age of the dinosaurs, according to a recent scientific report.  

The specimen dates to roughly 99 million years ago, when a tiny insect became encased in tree resin that later hardened into amber, preserving the creature in remarkable detail.  

Researchers from the School of Zoology and The Steinhardt Museum of Natural History examined the amber and formally described the new species as Cretodorus noonoo, nicknamed “Noo‑Noo.”
summary: Some 99 million years ago a tiny insect became trapped in tree resin that later hardened into amber. Researchers from the School of Zoology and The Steinhardt Museum of Natural History identified and described the new species Cretodorus noonoo, or "Noo-Noo."
author: Phys.org

title: Iced coffee does not predict job performance, may expose hiring bias
content:
An article titled “An iced coffee won’t predict job performance—but it might reveal hiring bias” points out that a candidate’s beverage choice is unrelated to their ability to do the job.  

The piece illustrates the issue with a hypothetical scenario: two equally qualified applicants interview for the same position, one carrying a bottle of water and the other an iced coffee.  

It asks whether such a superficial difference should influence hiring decisions.
summary: An iced coffee does not predict job performance. The difference between a candidate with water and one with an iced coffee could reveal bias in hiring.
author: Phys.org

title: Coastal forest loss in North Carolina's Albemarle‑Pamlico Peninsula accelerated after 2010
content:
A new study reports that forest loss along North Carolina’s coast is accelerating. Researchers found that the decline of coastal forests on the Albemarle‑Pamlico Peninsula began to speed up after 2010 and may still be increasing.

The analysis also showed that the state lost more than 20% of its coastal forest cover between 1985 and 2021.
summary: A new study shows coastal forest loss on North Carolina's Albemarle‑Pamlico Peninsula began accelerating after 2010 and may still be increasing. The research also reports that North Carolina lost more than 20% of its coastal forest between 1985 and 2021.
author: Phys.org

title: Labor's 2024 election win elevates early‑years and parental policy agenda
content:
Since Labor’s victory in the 2024 general election, the government has placed early‑years children and their parents higher on its political agenda. Policymakers are now focusing on children from birth to school age and on supporting families, a shift that has brought increased attention to childcare funding.

The heightened emphasis raises questions about whether additional funding for childcare will translate into higher workforce participation for mothers, a topic that is now under active discussion as part of Labor’s early‑years policy agenda.
summary: Since Labor won the 2024 general election, policy focused on children in the early years—from birth to school age—and their parents has moved sharply up the political agenda. This shift places early‑years and parental issues at the forefront of political discussion.
author: Phys.org

title: Study suggests quantum effects may lock early universe fields into current energy states
content:
A new study proposes that quantum interactions may have locked the early universe’s fields into existing energy states, effectively trapping the cosmos in its current configuration. The research, conducted by a scholar in the College of Engineering and Computer Science, seeks to explain why the universe appears unable to transition out of this “comfort zone.”

The study draws a parallel between the universe’s behavior and the quantum effects examined in efforts to preserve fragile information within quantum computers. According to the findings, the same types of quantum mechanisms that protect data in quantum computing could also prevent the universe’s fields from moving to alternative energy states.
summary: New research suggests the universe may be trapped in its own comfort zone. A researcher in the College of Engineering and Computer Science proposes that quantum effects akin to those used to preserve information in quantum computers could lock early‑universe fields into existing energy states.
author: Phys.org

title: Mathematicians say arXiv flooded with AI papers, new upload limit imposed
content:
Mathematicians have warned that the pre‑print repository arXiv is being overwhelmed by what they describe as “AI slop” papers, rendering the service virtually unusable for researchers.  

In response, arXiv has introduced a new limit on submissions, targeting “low‑value” uploads in an effort to curb the influx.
summary: Mathematicians warn that the pre‑print service arXiv is flooded with AI‑generated papers and has become virtually unusable. arXiv has responded by adding a new limit for uploaders.
author: New Scientist

title: 2026 Nobel Medicine Prize awarded to Deisseroth, Hegemann, Nagel for optogenetics
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their development of techniques that control brain cells with light, a breakthrough known as optogenetics.  

The trio’s work enables precise manipulation of neuronal activity, opening new avenues for research and potential therapies in neuroscience.
summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. They were recognized for developing techniques that control brain cells with light.
author: New Scientist

title: Record El Niño expected to cause wildfires, landslides and coral bleaching
content:
A record El Niño is expected to trigger a range of extreme weather events over the coming year, according to past trends. The phenomenon is projected to increase the risk of wildfires, landslides and coral bleaching.

Analysts note that despite these forecasts, the world is not prepared for the anticipated impacts.
summary: Past trends suggest the record El Niño will bring extreme weather including wildfires, landslides and coral bleaching. The world isn’t prepared for these impacts.
author: New Scientist

title: Pressing shin bones improves brain injury symptoms in mice and pigs
content:
Pressing down on the shin bones of animals with traumatic brain injuries was found to improve both cognitive and motor symptoms, according to a recent study. The intervention, which involves compressing the bones, appears to trigger the release of molecules that alleviate the effects of the injury.

The beneficial effects were observed in experiments using mice and pigs that had sustained traumatic brain injuries. Both species showed measurable improvements in brain‑related functions after the bone compression treatment.
summary: Pressing down on shin bones in mice and pigs with traumatic brain injuries improved cognitive and motor symptoms. The bone compression is thought to release molecules that ease the injuries.
author: New Scientist

title: Amateur uses AI to create largest rotationally symmetrical Venn diagrams
content:
An enduring mathematical problem—creating rotationally symmetrical Venn diagrams that grow in size—has been advanced by an amateur who employed artificial intelligence to produce the largest diagrams of this type to date.  

The AI-generated designs are noted for their baffling complexity and aesthetic appeal, pushing the boundaries of what has previously been achieved in symmetrical Venn diagram construction.  

This breakthrough demonstrates the potential of AI tools in tackling longstanding challenges in mathematical visualization.
summary: Creating rotationally symmetrical Venn diagrams of increasing size has been a long‑standing mathematical challenge. An amateur has used AI to generate the largest such diagrams, described as bafflingly complex and beautiful.
author: New Scientist

title: Boosting brain's glymphatic system studied to protect health and prevent Alzheimer’s
content:
Researchers are investigating whether enhancing the brain’s glymphatic system—a recently identified network that clears toxins—could help prevent Alzheimer’s disease. The inquiry follows growing interest in the system’s role in maintaining brain health.

Scientists report that new approaches are being explored to boost glymphatic function, aiming to improve the brain’s natural cleaning processes and protect against neurodegenerative damage. Ongoing studies seek to determine how such enhancements might translate into preventative strategies for Alzheimer’s.
summary: The glymphatic system is a recently discovered brain network that flushes out toxins. Scientists are investigating ways to enhance the system to protect brain health and potentially prevent Alzheimer’s.
author: New Scientist

title: DNA analysis of bone fragments from Denisova Cave identifies new extinct yak species
content:
Genetic analysis of hundreds of tiny bone fragments recovered from Denisova Cave has identified a previously unknown species of yak, indicating that the region once supported an extinct yak relative.  

The fragments were found in the same cave that produced the first fossil remains of the Denisovans, and DNA testing revealed the presence of this distinct yak lineage, expanding the known prehistoric fauna of the area.
summary: Genetic analysis of hundreds of tiny bone fragments from Denisova Cave was conducted. The results show the region once was home to a previously unknown species of yak.
author: New Scientist

title: Astronomers observe star consuming brown dwarf 300 light‑years away
content:
Astronomers have observed a star slowly consuming a brown dwarf located about 300 light‑years from Earth.  

The finding demonstrates a previously unrecognized mode of interaction between stars and their planetary‑mass companions.  

The discovery reveals a new way that stars and planetary companions can interact.
summary: Astronomers have observed a star slowly consuming a brown dwarf located about 300 light‑years from Earth. The finding suggests a new type of interaction between stars and planetary‑mass companions.
author: MIT News

title: Vagus nerve stimulation after practice boosts long‑term motor learning in mice
content:
Vagus nerve stimulation after training has been shown to strengthen long‑term motor learning in mice, according to a recent study. The researchers found that the effect appears during a critical window when the brain is still consolidating a new skill.

The improvement was associated with rhythmic changes in the brain’s blood vessels, suggesting that signals from the body can help prepare the brain for lasting neural change.
summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long‑term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill. The effect was linked to rhythmic changes in brain blood vessels, hinting that body‑to‑brain signals may help prepare the brain for lasting change.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA selects GIMLI project to probe Marius Hill Pit for possible underground cave
content:
NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit on the Moon opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube.  

The investigation will employ radar, seismic sensors, gravity measurements and cameras to search beneath the lunar surface and estimate the size of any hidden void.  

Researchers say such caves could preserve clues to the Moon’s volcanic history and potentially provide protected shelters for future astronauts.
summary: NASA has selected the GIMLI project to investigate whether the Marius Hill Pit opens into a vast underground cave or lava tube. Researchers will use radar, seismic sensors, gravity measurements and cameras to search beneath the lunar surface and estimate the size of any hidden void.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists detail effects of seven-day fasting on human body
content:
Scientists have shown that a week of fasting induces widespread physiological changes in the human body. The study found that while many effects begin to emerge after about three days without food, the full spectrum of changes unfolds over the entire seven‑day period.

The research indicates that prolonged fasting triggers major alterations throughout the body, with the most striking responses appearing after roughly three days of abstaining from food. These findings highlight the depth of the body's adaptation to extended periods of nutrient deprivation.

The results suggest that fasting may influence health in ways that go beyond weight loss and could eventually inspire treatments that mimic its effects.
summary: Scientists found that prolonged fasting triggers major changes throughout the body, with many of the most interesting effects appearing after about three days without food. The findings suggest fasting may affect health beyond weight loss and could eventually inspire treatments that mimic its effects.
author: Science Daily

title: October sky: Saturn opposition, Orionid meteors from Halley's Comet, Moon near Pleiades
content:
October skywatchers are invited to observe several celestial events. Saturn reaches opposition, making it visible throughout the night, while meteors from Halley’s Comet will appear during the Orionid peak. The Moon will also pass near the Pleiades star cluster.

Astronomers note that moonlight could mask some Orionid meteors, but the optimal viewing window is before dawn after the Moon has set.
summary: In October, skywatchers can see Saturn at opposition and watch the Moon sweep past the Pleiades star cluster. The Orionid meteor shower, produced by Halley’s Comet debris, peaks before dawn after the Moon sets, though moonlight may obscure some meteors.
author: Science Daily

title: Saturn at opposition on Oct. 4 offers best view as it nears closest approach this year
content:
Saturn appears as a moderately bright, creamy‑white object that can be seen with the naked eye. This week offers an excellent opportunity to locate the giant planet in the night sky.

The planet reached opposition on 4 October, placing Earth almost directly between Saturn and the Sun. In this configuration, Saturn rises as the Sun sets, remains visible throughout the night, and sets around sunrise.

At opposition, Saturn is also at its closest point to Earth for the year.
summary: Saturn appears as a moderately bright, creamy‑white object that is easily visible to the naked eye. It reached opposition on 4 October, placing Earth almost directly between the Sun and Saturn and putting the planet at about its closest point to Earth for the year, so it rises at sunset and stays visible through the night.
author: Guardian Science

title: Review of Paul D. MacLean's 1959 triune brain model and the “lizard brain” myth
content:
The notion of a “lizard brain” hidden beneath our rational mind has long appealed to popular imagination, yet neuroscientists say the biological reality differs from the metaphor.  

In 1959, Paul D. MacLean introduced the “triune” brain model—a three‑in‑one concept that posits three distinct brain structures stacked within the skull, each competing to shape feelings and thoughts. The model quickly became one of the most recognized ideas in human biology, reflecting a broader cultural fascination with the number three seen in stories, slogans and philosophical frameworks.  

MacLean’s triune theory illustrates how neuroscience, like other fields, can be drawn to triadic explanations, even as ongoing research continues to refine our understanding of brain evolution and function.
summary: In 1959 Paul D. MacLean proposed a “triune” model describing three distinct brains layered inside the skull. The model quickly became one of the best‑known and most enduring concepts in human biology.
author: Guardian Science

title: Global study finds women report more pain than men across all body areas
content:
A major global study has found that women report experiencing more pain than men across the whole body.  

Researchers examined pain patterns worldwide and across the human lifespan, noting that the steepest increase in reported pain occurs before age 55. The study measured multiple types of pain and found that women reported higher levels of pain than men for every category assessed.  

The findings arrive amid ongoing concern about a gender pain gap, in which women are less likely to be prescribed the pain relief they need.
summary: Researchers conducting a worldwide study across the lifespan found that women report higher levels of pain than men for all types measured. The study noted the steepest rise in reported pain occurs before age 55 and highlighted concerns that women are less likely to be prescribed needed pain relief.
author: Guardian Science

title: Nobel Medicine 2026 awarded for light‑gated ion channel and optogenetics research
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to three researchers for their work on the mysteries of the brain. Karl Deisseroth of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, Peter Hegemann of the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg will each receive a share of the 12 million Swedish‑krona prize.

The laureates were honored “for their discoveries concerning light‑gated ion channels and optogenetics,” a technique that uses light to control neuronal activity. Their contributions are recognized as advancing understanding of brain function.
summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to three scientists for their work on light‑gated ion channels and optogenetics. Karl Deisseroth of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, Peter Hegemann of the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg will share the 12m Swedish kronor prize.
author: Guardian Science

title: Second‑generation planet may solve NASA Hubble cold case
content:
A new analysis of archival Hubble Space Telescope data suggests that a suspected second‑generation planet may resolve a long‑standing NASA Hubble “cold case.”  

The study indicates that “dead” white dwarf stars could host planetary systems that formed after the stars’ original evolution, pointing to the possibility of second‑generation planets orbiting these remnants.  

If confirmed, the finding would provide a plausible explanation for the previously unexplained observations associated with the Hubble data set.
summary: New analysis of archival Hubble data suggests that dead white dwarf stars could host second‑generation planetary systems. The suspected second‑generation planet is seen as a possible solution to a NASA Hubble cold case.
author: NASA News

title: NASA upgrades testing to combat supercooled large droplet icing hazard
content:
NASA is applying its expertise and upgrading its test facilities to tackle a rare but persistent aviation hazard known as supercooled large droplet icing. The phenomenon occurs when aircraft fly through clouds that contain unusually large, very cold water droplets, leading to ice buildup on the airframe.  

The agency’s testing efforts aim to improve safety by better understanding and mitigating the risks associated with these large supercooled droplets.
summary: NASA is leveraging its expertise and enhancing test facilities to address supercooled large droplet icing, a rare aviation hazard. The hazard occurs when aircraft encounter unusually large, very cold water droplets in clouds.
author: NASA News

title: NASA to stream live SpaceX Crew-12 undocking and splashdown on Oct. 7
content:
NASA announced that it will stream the return and splashdown of the SpaceX Crew‑12 mission live for the public.  

The agency and SpaceX are targeting an undocking no earlier than 8:05 a.m. EDT on Wednesday, Oct. 7, from the International Space Station, contingent on weather conditions. The crew slated for the departure includes NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev.  

The live broadcast will follow the undocking and subsequent splashdown, providing viewers with real‑time coverage of the mission’s final phase.
summary: NASA and SpaceX plan to undock the Crew-12 mission from the International Space Station at no earlier than 8:05 a.m. EDT on Oct. 7, pending weather. The crew includes NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev.
author: NASA News

title: Opus 5.5 agents discover two room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates
content:
Opus 5.5 agents have identified two candidates for room‑temperature magnetic semiconductors, according to a post on the Vals.Ai blog.

The discovery was shared via the blog at https://www.Vals.Ai/blogs/room-temperature-magnetic-semiconductors and generated discussion on Hacker News (https://news.Ycombinator.Com/item?Id=49970667), where the thread received 115 points and 96 comments.
